title: Code Practice — C# Focused (16 Weeks)
recurringNote: The solution log is added to every week as a fixed task; Thursday re-solve day picks problems from this log.

weeks.title: Warm-up: Accounts and Baseline
weeks.summary: Set up all platforms and start your solution log. Take a baseline test so you can measure your progress later.

tasks.text: Create free accounts on CodeWars (https://www.codewars.com), Exercism (https://exercism.org), HackerRank (https://www.hackerrank.com) and LeetCode (https://leetcode.com). Then solve two 8-kyu C# katas on CodeWars (https://www.codewars.com/kata/search/csharp) (30-40 min)
Go to the Exercism Python track (https://exercism.org/tracks/python). Solve 2 easy exercises in Python (30-40 min)
Go to HackerRank SQL (https://www.hackerrank.com/domains/sql). Solve 3-4 problems from the "Basic Select" section (30-40 min)

🔁 Start your solution log: create a simple note file. For each problem, write the problem name, the language, and a one-line approach. Then re-solve one of Monday's C# katas, but this time in Python. Compare your solution with the top-voted solutions on CodeWars and note one trick you learned (30-40 min)

⏱️ BASELINE TEST: solve 1 LeetCode Easy problem (https://leetcode.com/problemset/) in C# with a 25-minute timer. Record your time and result in your log. This is your day-0 measurement — you will compare it at Week 8 and Week 16 (30-40 min)
Solution log: after each solved problem, add one line — problem name, language, one-line approach. Thursday re-solve day and season reviews pick from this log (5 min/day)

weeks.title: First Steps Up: 7-kyu and Dart
weeks.summary: Move up to 7-kyu katas and add Dart to your rotation. Start your first Flutter codelab on Saturday.
weeks.source: CodeWars C# (https://www.codewars.com/kata/search/csharp), Exercism Dart (https://exercism.org/tracks/dart), HackerRank SQL (https://www.hackerrank.com/domains/sql), Flutter codelabs (https://docs.flutter.dev/codelabs)

tasks.text: Solve two 7-kyu C# katas on CodeWars (https://www.codewars.com/kata/search/csharp). Add them to your solution log (30-40 min)
Go to the Exercism Dart track (https://exercism.org/tracks/dart). Solve 2 easy exercises in Dart (30-40 min)
On HackerRank SQL (https://www.hackerrank.com/domains/sql), solve 3-4 problems from the "Aggregation" section (30-40 min)

🔁 RE-SOLVE day: pick one problem from your solution log (from Week 1). Solve it again in a different language than before. Then compare your solution with the top-voted solutions on the platform and note one trick you learned (30-40 min)
🛠️ Mini-project: open the Flutter codelabs page (https://docs.flutter.dev/codelabs) and start "Write your first Flutter app". Do session 1 only — stop when your time is up (30-40 min)
Solution log: after each solved problem, add one line — problem name, language, one-line approach. Thursday re-solve day and season reviews pick from this log (5 min/day)

weeks.title: Joins and Timed Practice
weeks.summary: Keep the 7-kyu level and learn SQL joins. On Saturday, do your first real timed session with two problems.
weeks.source: CodeWars C# (https://www.codewars.com/kata/search/csharp), Exercism Python (https://exercism.org/tracks/python), HackerRank SQL (https://www.hackerrank.com/domains/sql), LeetCode (https://leetcode.com/problemset/)

tasks.text: Solve two 7-kyu C# katas on CodeWars (https://www.codewars.com/kata/search/csharp). Add them to your solution log (30-40 min)
On the Exercism Python track (https://exercism.org/tracks/python), solve 2 exercises in Python (30-40 min)
On HackerRank SQL (https://www.hackerrank.com/domains/sql), solve 3-4 problems from the "Basic Join" section (30-40 min)

🔁 RE-SOLVE day: pick one problem from your solution log (a past week). Solve it again in a different language than before. Compare with the top-voted solutions and note one trick you learned (30-40 min)
⏱️ TIMED TEST: solve 2 LeetCode Easy problems (https://leetcode.com/problemset/) in C#, 25 minutes each. Record your times and results in your log (30-40 min)
Solution log: after each solved problem, add one line — problem name, language, one-line approach. Thursday re-solve day and season reviews pick from this log (5 min/day)

weeks.title: Level Up and First Mentor Feedback
weeks.summary: Try your first 6-kyu kata and ask for free human feedback on Exercism. This feedback loop is a key part of the plan.
weeks.source: CodeWars C# (https://www.codewars.com/kata/search/csharp), Exercism C# (https://exercism.org/tracks/csharp), Exercism Dart (https://exercism.org/tracks/dart), HackerRank SQL (https://www.hackerrank.com/domains/sql), Flutter codelabs (https://docs.flutter.dev/codelabs)

tasks.text: Solve one 7-kyu and one 6-kyu C# kata on CodeWars (https://www.codewars.com/kata/search/csharp). Add them to your solution log (30-40 min)
On the Exercism Dart track (https://exercism.org/tracks/dart), solve 2 exercises in Dart (30-40 min)
On HackerRank SQL (https://www.hackerrank.com/domains/sql), solve 3-4 problems from the "Advanced Join" section (30-40 min)

🔁 RE-SOLVE day: pick one problem from your log and solve it again in a different language. ALSO: submit one solution on the Exercism C# track (https://exercism.org/tracks/csharp) and request FREE human mentoring on it. A real mentor will review your code — this is the plan's feedback loop (30-40 min)
🛠️ Mini-project: continue "Write your first Flutter app" on the Flutter codelabs page (https://docs.flutter.dev/codelabs). Do session 2 (30-40 min)
Solution log: after each solved problem, add one line — problem name, language, one-line approach. Thursday re-solve day and season reviews pick from this log (5 min/day)

weeks.title: 6-kyu Zone and SQL on LeetCode
weeks.summary: Work fully at 6-kyu level now. Try SQL problems on LeetCode and attempt your first Medium problem.
weeks.source: CodeWars C# (https://www.codewars.com/kata/search/csharp), Exercism Python (https://exercism.org/tracks/python), LeetCode Database (https://leetcode.com/problemset/database/), LeetCode (https://leetcode.com/problemset/)

tasks.text: Solve two 6-kyu C# katas on CodeWars (https://www.codewars.com/kata/search/csharp). Add them to your solution log (30-40 min)
On the Exercism Python track (https://exercism.org/tracks/python), solve 2 exercises in Python (30-40 min)
Go to LeetCode Database (https://leetcode.com/problemset/database/). Solve 2 Easy SQL problems (30-40 min)
🔁 RE-SOLVE day: pick one problem from your log (a past week). Solve it again in a different language than before. Compare with the top-voted solutions and note one trick you learned (30-40 min)

⏱️ TIMED TEST: solve 1 LeetCode Easy in C#, then attempt 1 Medium (https://leetcode.com/problemset/) with a 35-minute timer. It is OK if you do not finish the Medium — record how far you got (30-40 min)
Solution log: after each solved problem, add one line — problem name, language, one-line approach. Thursday re-solve day and season reviews pick from this log (5 min/day)

weeks.title: PostgreSQL Practice and Frontend Build
weeks.summary: Practice SQL on pgexercises for a different style of drills. On Saturday, start a small frontend build with HTML/CSS/Bootstrap.
weeks.source: CodeWars C# (https://www.codewars.com/kata/search/csharp), Exercism Dart (https://exercism.org/tracks/dart), pgexercises (https://pgexercises.com/), Frontend Mentor (https://www.frontendmentor.io/challenges)

tasks.text: Solve two 6-kyu C# katas on CodeWars (https://www.codewars.com/kata/search/csharp). Add them to your solution log (30-40 min)
On the Exercism Dart track (https://exercism.org/tracks/dart), solve 2 exercises in Dart (30-40 min)
Go to pgexercises (https://pgexercises.com/). Work through the "Basic" section, and start "Aggregates" if you have time (30-40 min)
🔁 RE-SOLVE day: pick one problem from your log and solve it again in a different language than before. Compare with the top-voted solutions and note one trick you learned (30-40 min)

🛠️ Mini-project: pick one FREE challenge on Frontend Mentor (https://www.frontendmentor.io/challenges). Part 1: build the page layout with HTML, CSS and Bootstrap. You will not finish it today — that is fine (30-40 min)
Solution log: after each solved problem, add one line — problem name, language, one-line approach. Thursday re-solve day and season reviews pick from this log (5 min/day)

weeks.title: Weak-Spot Review and Medium Challenge
weeks.summary: Use your solution log to find your weakest SQL topic and fix it. On Saturday, take on a full LeetCode Medium under time pressure.
weeks.source: CodeWars C# (https://www.codewars.com/kata/search/csharp), Exercism Python (https://exercism.org/tracks/python), HackerRank SQL (https://www.hackerrank.com/domains/sql), pgexercises (https://pgexercises.com/), LeetCode (https://leetcode.com/problemset/)

tasks.text: Solve two 6-kyu C# katas on CodeWars (https://www.codewars.com/kata/search/csharp). Add them to your solution log (30-40 min)
On the Exercism Python track (https://exercism.org/tracks/python), solve 2 exercises in Python (30-40 min)

SQL mixed review: look at your solution log and find your weakest SQL topic. Solve 3-4 problems on that topic, on HackerRank SQL (https://www.hackerrank.com/domains/sql) or pgexercises (https://pgexercises.com/) (30-40 min)
🔁 RE-SOLVE day: pick one problem from your log (a past week). Solve it again in a different language than before. Compare with the top-voted solutions and note one trick you learned (30-40 min)
⏱️ TIMED TEST: solve 1 LeetCode Medium (https://leetcode.com/problemset/) in C# with a 35-minute timer. Record your time and result in your log (30-40 min)
Solution log: after each solved problem, add one line — problem name, language, one-line approach. Thursday re-solve day and season reviews pick from this log (5 min/day)

weeks.title: Season Final: Certification Week
weeks.summary: Review your whole season, apply your mentor's feedback, and finish with a free timed C# certification. Goal: reach 6 kyu on CodeWars.
weeks.source: CodeWars C# (https://www.codewars.com/kata/search/csharp), Exercism Dart (https://exercism.org/tracks/dart), Exercism C# (https://exercism.org/tracks/csharp), HackerRank SQL (https://www.hackerrank.com/domains/sql), HackerRank Skills Certification (https://www.hackerrank.com/skills-verification)

tasks.text: Solve one light 6-kyu C# kata on CodeWars (https://www.codewars.com/kata/search/csharp). Then read your whole solution log and mark the 3 hardest problems of the season (30-40 min)
On the Exercism Dart track (https://exercism.org/tracks/dart), solve 2 exercises in Dart (30-40 min)
SQL review for the certification: on HackerRank SQL (https://www.hackerrank.com/domains/sql), re-solve one problem each from Select, Aggregation and Join. Work fast — this is exam warm-up (30-40 min)

🔁 Check the Exercism mentor's reply on your C# solution (https://exercism.org/tracks/csharp). Read the feedback carefully and apply it to one old solution from your log. Write in your log what you changed and why (30-40 min)

🏁 SEASON 1 FINAL: take the FREE timed HackerRank "C# (Basic)" Skills Certification (https://www.hackerrank.com/skills-verification). After the test, record your CodeWars rank in your log. Season goal: reach 6 kyu (30-40 min)
Solution log: after each solved problem, add one line — problem name, language, one-line approach. Thursday re-solve day and season reviews pick from this log (5 min/day)

weeks.title: Arrays & Hashing
weeks.summary: Start Season 2 with the first NeetCode pattern: Arrays & Hashing. This pattern is the base for many interview problems. You also start the weekly rhythm: pattern, kata, SQL, re-solve, and a timed test.
weeks.source: NeetCode roadmap (https://neetcode.io/roadmap), LeetCode (https://leetcode.com/problemset/), Exercism Python (https://exercism.org/tracks/python), HackerRank SQL (https://www.hackerrank.com/domains/sql)

tasks.text: Open the NeetCode roadmap (https://neetcode.io/roadmap) and go to the "Arrays & Hashing" pattern. Solve 2 problems from this list in C# on LeetCode (https://leetcode.com/problemset/). If you get stuck, watch the free video solution. Write both problems in your solution log (30-40 min)
Python kata day. Go to Exercism Python (https://exercism.org/tracks/python) and solve 1-2 exercises. Read the community solutions after you finish and note one new idea (30-40 min)
SQL day. Go to HackerRank SQL (https://www.hackerrank.com/domains/sql) and solve 2-3 problems from the Intermediate level. Focus on JOIN and GROUP BY questions (30-40 min)

🔁 RE-SOLVE day. Pick one problem from your solution log and solve it again in a DIFFERENT language (for example: first time C#, now Python). Then compare your code with the top solutions and write down one trick you learned (30-40 min)

⏱️ TIMED test. On LeetCode (https://leetcode.com/problemset/), pick 2 problems from the Arrays & Hashing pattern that you have NOT solved before. Set a timer: 30 minutes for each problem. Write the results in your log (30-40 min)
Solution log: after each solved problem, add one line — problem name, language, one-line approach. Thursday re-solve day and season reviews pick from this log (5 min/day)

weeks.title: Two Pointers
weeks.summary: This week you learn the Two Pointers pattern. It is a simple but powerful idea: move two indexes through the data. On Saturday you start the season project: a small Flutter flashcard app for your English vocabulary.
weeks.source: NeetCode roadmap (https://neetcode.io/roadmap), Exercism Dart (https://exercism.org/tracks/dart), LeetCode Database (https://leetcode.com/problemset/database/), Flutter codelabs (https://docs.flutter.dev/codelabs)

tasks.text: Open the NeetCode roadmap (https://neetcode.io/roadmap) and go to the "Two Pointers" pattern. Solve 1-2 problems from this list in C# on LeetCode (https://leetcode.com/problemset/). Add them to your solution log (30-40 min)
Dart kata day. Go to Exercism Dart (https://exercism.org/tracks/dart) and solve 1-2 exercises. Dart practice also helps your Flutter project this Saturday (30-40 min)
SQL day. Go to LeetCode Database (https://leetcode.com/problemset/database/) and solve 1-2 Medium problems. Read the discussion tab after you finish (30-40 min)
🔁 RE-SOLVE day. Pick one problem from your solution log and solve it again in a DIFFERENT language. Compare your code with the top solutions and note one trick (30-40 min)

🛠️ PROJECT session 1. Create the skeleton of your Flutter flashcard app: one screen, a hardcoded English word list, and a basic card UI that shows a word. Use the Flutter codelabs as reference (https://docs.flutter.dev/codelabs). Goal: the app runs and shows cards (30-40 min)
Solution log: after each solved problem, add one line — problem name, language, one-line approach. Thursday re-solve day and season reviews pick from this log (5 min/day)

weeks.title: Sliding Window
weeks.summary: The Sliding Window pattern builds on Two Pointers. You use it for problems about subarrays and substrings. SQL day moves to pgexercises for aggregate practice.
weeks.source: NeetCode roadmap (https://neetcode.io/roadmap), Exercism Python (https://exercism.org/tracks/python), pgexercises (https://pgexercises.com/), LeetCode (https://leetcode.com/problemset/)

tasks.text: Open the NeetCode roadmap (https://neetcode.io/roadmap) and go to the "Sliding Window" pattern. Solve 1-2 problems from this list in C# on LeetCode (https://leetcode.com/problemset/). Watch the video solution if you need help (30-40 min)
Python kata day. Go to Exercism Python (https://exercism.org/tracks/python) and solve 1-2 exercises. Try to write a shorter solution than your first idea (30-40 min)
SQL day. Go to pgexercises (https://pgexercises.com/) and work through the "Aggregates" section. Solve as many exercises as you can in the time (30-40 min)
🔁 RE-SOLVE day. Pick one problem from your solution log and solve it again in a DIFFERENT language. Compare with the top solutions and note one trick (30-40 min)

⏱️ TIMED test. On LeetCode (https://leetcode.com/problemset/), pick 1 Medium problem from the Sliding Window pattern that you have NOT solved before. Set a timer: 35 minutes. No pauses. Write the result in your log (30-40 min)
Solution log: after each solved problem, add one line — problem name, language, one-line approach. Thursday re-solve day and season reviews pick from this log (5 min/day)

weeks.title: Stack
weeks.summary: This week is about the Stack pattern: last in, first out. On Thursday you also send one Exercism solution for free human mentoring. On Saturday you add state to your Flutter app.
weeks.source: NeetCode roadmap (https://neetcode.io/roadmap), Exercism Dart (https://exercism.org/tracks/dart), HackerRank SQL (https://www.hackerrank.com/domains/sql), LeetCode (https://leetcode.com/problemset/)

tasks.text: Open the NeetCode roadmap (https://neetcode.io/roadmap) and go to the "Stack" pattern. Solve 1-2 problems from this list in C# on LeetCode (https://leetcode.com/problemset/). Add them to your solution log (30-40 min)
Dart kata day. Go to Exercism Dart (https://exercism.org/tracks/dart) and solve 1-2 exercises (30-40 min)
SQL day. Go to HackerRank SQL (https://www.hackerrank.com/domains/sql) and solve 2-3 more Intermediate problems. Pick topics you have not tried yet (30-40 min)

🔁 RE-SOLVE day. Pick one problem from your solution log and solve it again in a DIFFERENT language. ALSO: on Exercism, submit one of your solutions for free human mentoring (click "Request mentoring"). A real person will review your code (30-40 min)

🛠️ PROJECT session 2. Add state to your Flutter flashcard app: the user can mark a word as known or unknown, and there is simple navigation between screens (for example: card screen and word list screen). Goal: tapping a button changes the word status (30-40 min)
Solution log: after each solved problem, add one line — problem name, language, one-line approach. Thursday re-solve day and season reviews pick from this log (5 min/day)

weeks.title: Binary Search
weeks.summary: Binary Search is one of the most common interview patterns. The idea is simple, but the details (borders, middle index) need care. Saturday is a timed test again.
weeks.source: NeetCode roadmap (https://neetcode.io/roadmap), Exercism Python (https://exercism.org/tracks/python), HackerRank SQL (https://www.hackerrank.com/domains/sql), LeetCode (https://leetcode.com/problemset/)

tasks.text: Open the NeetCode roadmap (https://neetcode.io/roadmap) and go to the "Binary Search" pattern. Solve 1-2 problems from this list in C# on LeetCode (https://leetcode.com/problemset/). Be careful with the left/right border logic (30-40 min)
Python kata day. Go to Exercism Python (https://exercism.org/tracks/python) and solve 1-2 exercises. Check if a mentor answered your Hafta 12 request; if yes, read the feedback (30-40 min)
SQL day. Go to HackerRank SQL (https://www.hackerrank.com/domains/sql) and solve 2-3 Intermediate problems. Try one problem with a subquery (30-40 min)
🔁 RE-SOLVE day. Pick one problem from your solution log and solve it again in a DIFFERENT language. Compare with the top solutions and note one trick (30-40 min)
⏱️ TIMED test. On LeetCode (https://leetcode.com/problemset/), pick 1 Medium binary search problem that you have NOT solved before. Set a timer: 30 minutes. Write the result in your log (30-40 min)
Solution log: after each solved problem, add one line — problem name, language, one-line approach. Thursday re-solve day and season reviews pick from this log (5 min/day)

weeks.title: Linked List
weeks.summary: The Linked List pattern teaches pointer manipulation: reverse a list, find the middle, detect a cycle. On Saturday your Flutter app learns to save data, so the word list survives an app restart.
weeks.source: NeetCode roadmap (https://neetcode.io/roadmap), Exercism Dart (https://exercism.org/tracks/dart), LeetCode Database (https://leetcode.com/problemset/database/), LeetCode (https://leetcode.com/problemset/)

tasks.text: Open the NeetCode roadmap (https://neetcode.io/roadmap) and go to the "Linked List" pattern. Solve 1-2 problems from this list in C# on LeetCode (https://leetcode.com/problemset/). Draw the pointers on paper if it helps (30-40 min)
Dart kata day. Go to Exercism Dart (https://exercism.org/tracks/dart) and solve 1-2 exercises (30-40 min)
SQL day. Go to LeetCode Database (https://leetcode.com/problemset/database/) and solve 1-2 Medium problems. Compare your query with the fastest solutions (30-40 min)
🔁 RE-SOLVE day. Pick one problem from your solution log and solve it again in a DIFFERENT language. Compare with the top solutions and note one trick (30-40 min)

🛠️ PROJECT session 3. Add local storage to your Flutter flashcard app: save the word list and the known/unknown status with shared_preferences or a similar package. Goal: close the app, open it again, and the data is still there (30-40 min)
Solution log: after each solved problem, add one line — problem name, language, one-line approach. Thursday re-solve day and season reviews pick from this log (5 min/day)

weeks.title: Trees (intro)
weeks.summary: A soft introduction to trees: only easy problems this week. Trees are a big topic; the goal now is to feel comfortable with recursion and traversal. Saturday is a mini mock interview.
weeks.source: NeetCode roadmap (https://neetcode.io/roadmap), Exercism Python (https://exercism.org/tracks/python), HackerRank SQL (https://www.hackerrank.com/domains/sql), LeetCode (https://leetcode.com/problemset/)

tasks.text: Open the NeetCode roadmap (https://neetcode.io/roadmap) and go to the "Trees" pattern. Solve 1-2 EASY problems only (for example: Invert Binary Tree, Maximum Depth) in C# on LeetCode (https://leetcode.com/problemset/) (30-40 min)
Python kata day. Go to Exercism Python (https://exercism.org/tracks/python) and solve 1-2 exercises (30-40 min)

SQL day. Go to HackerRank SQL (https://www.hackerrank.com/domains/sql) and try 1-2 problems from the Advanced topics (Advanced Select or Advanced Join). It is OK if they feel hard; that is the point (30-40 min)
🔁 RE-SOLVE day. Pick one problem from your solution log and solve it again in a DIFFERENT language. Compare with the top solutions and note one trick (30-40 min)

⏱️ Mini mock interview. On LeetCode (https://leetcode.com/problemset/), pick 2 problems you have NOT solved: 1 Easy and 1 Medium. Set a timer: 60 minutes total, no pauses, no hints. This simulates a real interview. Write the results in your log (60 min, plan extra time today)
Solution log: after each solved problem, add one line — problem name, language, one-line approach. Thursday re-solve day and season reviews pick from this log (5 min/day)

weeks.title: Finals
weeks.summary: The last week of Season 2. You review your weakest pattern, close open feedback, and finish with the season finals: two free HackerRank certifications, a working flashcard app, and a comparison with your Season 1 baseline.
weeks.source: NeetCode roadmap (https://neetcode.io/roadmap), Exercism (https://exercism.org/), HackerRank skills verification (https://www.hackerrank.com/skills-verification), LeetCode (https://leetcode.com/problemset/)

tasks.text: Check your solution log and find your WEAKEST pattern from this season (most fails or slowest times). Solve 2 problems from that pattern on the NeetCode roadmap (https://neetcode.io/roadmap) in C# on LeetCode (https://leetcode.com/problemset/) (30-40 min)
Free-choice kata. Go to Exercism (https://exercism.org/) and solve 1-2 exercises in your favorite language (Python, Dart, or C#). Enjoy it; you earned it (30-40 min)

SQL certification prep. Review the Intermediate topics on HackerRank SQL (https://www.hackerrank.com/domains/sql): joins, aggregates, subqueries. Re-solve 1-2 problems you found hard before. This prepares you for Saturday (30-40 min)

Final log review. Read your whole Season 2 solution log: which tricks did you note? Which patterns are strong now? Also apply the last mentor feedback from Exercism if anything is still open (30-40 min)

🏁 SEASON 2 FINALS. Go to HackerRank skills verification (https://www.hackerrank.com/skills-verification) and take the FREE timed certifications: "Problem Solving (Basic)" AND "SQL (Intermediate)". Then finish the flashcard app: it should run and save data. Finally, redo your Hafta 1 baseline problem and compare your time with Season 1. Celebrate the season (plan extra time today, ~90 min)
Solution log: after each solved problem, add one line — problem name, language, one-line approach. Thursday re-solve day and season reviews pick from this log (5 min/day)
